quote: The perceived trustworthiness of AI systems decreased over time from 63 percent of people viewing AI systems as trustworthy in 2022 to 56 percent in 2024
why: Read from the primary PDF, page 37. The numbers 63 and 56 are right but the year is 2024, not 2023, and the metric is perceived trustworthiness, not willingness to trust: willingness to rely fell 52 percent to 43 percent.

quote: Figure 16: Trust of AI systems and worry about AI in 2022 and 2024
why: The report's own figure title dates the comparison 2022 to 2024, so calling it a 2022 to 2023 drop is wrong.

quote: rising from almost half (49%) of respondents in 2022 to 62 percent in 2024
why: Same year error: the second wave is 2024, not 2023, though the percentages themselves are accurate.

quote: 48,340 people completed the survey across 47 countries and jurisdictions
why: Sample size, country count, the 66 percent regular use and the 46 percent willing to trust all check out; only 'late 2024' is loose, since fieldwork ran to mid-January 2025.

quote: People in advanced economies are less trusting (39% vs. 57%) and accepting (65% vs. 84%) compared to emerging economies.
why: The real figures are 57 percent and 39 percent, not the 60 and 40 the document prints as if quoted.

quote: People in advanced economies are less trusting (39% vs. 57%) and accepting (65% vs. 84%) compared to emerging economies.
why: The emerging versus advanced split comes from the 2025 report and reads 57 versus 39, so attributing a 60 versus 40 gap to a 2023 news piece is wrong twice over.
